case_policy: Cases are bounded primary-source records. Vendor-reported outcomes remain attributed; standards examples are patterns rather than outcome claims; FieldOps Relay is fictional synthesis.

cases.name: Anthropic multi-agent research system
cases.problem: Research questions benefit from exploring many independent information paths and synthesizing them.
cases.context: Anthropic's Research feature and its provider stack.
constraints: Parallel agents consume substantially more tokens
Coordination and delegation quality affect results
cases.architecture: Lead agent delegates to parallel subagents, subagents search independently, and results return for synthesis with evaluation and production controls.
cases.approach: Task decomposition, parallel search, explicit prompting/tool design, evaluation and operational debugging.
cases.tradeoffs: Reported quality gains are exchanged for higher token use, coordination complexity and latency/cost considerations.
failures: Poor delegation can omit useful paths
Synthesis can lose or misweight evidence
cases.outcomes: Use only the metrics and qualitative outcomes reported in the source, attributed to Anthropic's research workload.
cases.lessons: Multi-agent topology is a workload hypothesis to test, not a maturity level.
cases.fieldops_use: Satellite contrast for AR-07: parallel manual/inventory investigation is compared with one agent; no Anthropic metric is copied into the synthetic result.
cases.limitations: No independent reproduction; provider-selected model, harness and evaluation; not evidence for effectful service coordination.

cases.name: OpenAI in-house data agent
cases.problem: Employees need to answer data questions across organizational data and analytical context.
cases.context: OpenAI's internal data systems and access controls.
constraints: Need for trustworthy queries and answers
cases.architecture: Agent with tools and contextual resources over internal data infrastructure, permissions and an evaluation/feedback process.
cases.approach: Curate context and tool surface, honor permissions, evaluate behavior and improve from feedback.
cases.tradeoffs: Richer context and tools improve reach but increase permission, freshness, provenance and evaluation obligations.
cases.outcomes: Only qualitative/provider-reported outcomes may be used, clearly attributed.
cases.lessons: Context and tool access are engineered system components, not model properties.
cases.fieldops_use: Satellite contrast for AR-06 and AR-09: data-agent read access is compared with FieldOps' proposed/effectful capabilities.
cases.limitations: Internal case, no independent audit, organization-specific infrastructure, not a general data-agent blueprint.

cases.name: OpenAI internal coding-agent monitoring
cases.problem: Internal coding agents can take many repository/tool actions and need detection and response for concerning behavior.
cases.context: OpenAI's internal coding-agent deployment and monitoring stack.
cases.architecture: Layered automated monitoring plus human review and response procedures around agent activity.
cases.approach: Monitor trajectories/signals, triage flagged behavior, investigate and feed operational learning back into controls.
cases.tradeoffs: More monitoring improves visibility but adds privacy, access, retention, reviewer-load and blind-spot risks.
cases.outcomes: Report only provider-described deployment evidence; do not claim elimination of misalignment.
cases.lessons: Trace data needs a decision and response path; collection alone is not a control.
cases.fieldops_use: Satellite contrast for AR-11/AR-12: design a privacy-aware alert-to-response path for synthetic reservations.
cases.limitations: Provider-authored, internal environment, monitor performance does not transfer automatically.

cases.name: Operator and ChatGPT agent confirmation controls
cases.problem: A browser-acting agent can make mistakes or be manipulated while performing state-changing actions.
cases.architecture: Layered mitigations including confirmation before selected actions, active supervision/watch modes, models/monitors and restricted contexts.
cases.approach: Classify consequential actions, interrupt before execution, expose evidence to the user and monitor for risks.
cases.tradeoffs: Confirmations add friction and can be habituated; coverage boundaries and timing matter.
cases.outcomes: Use system-card evaluation results only with their test conditions and provider attribution.
cases.lessons: Human confirmation is one layer and must be bound to the proposed effect; it is not blanket safety proof.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-02/AR-08 contrast: reservation approval displays exact part/slot, consequence, expiry and evidence before local synthetic effect.
cases.limitations: Product-specific controls and evaluation; formal organizational authorization is outside the system card.

cases.name: AWS idempotent API design
cases.problem: Clients cannot always tell whether a timed-out state-changing request completed, and retries can duplicate effects.
cases.context: AWS API design and large-scale distributed service operations.
constraints: Same parameters can represent different intent
cases.architecture: Client-supplied request identifiers, server-side duplicate detection, semantic validation, bounded backoff/jitter and audit records.
cases.approach: Make intended idempotency explicit, reconcile ambiguous results and coordinate retry layers.
cases.tradeoffs: Deduplication state and retention cost; identifiers cannot define semantic intent alone; not every effect is reversible.
cases.outcomes: Engineering pattern only; no cross-workload performance claim is imported.
cases.lessons: Agent-selected actions inherit ordinary distributed-systems ambiguity and add no exemption from effect semantics.
cases.fieldops_use: Core AR-04/AR-08 injection: synthetic reservation succeeds but the response is lost; ledger reconciliation prevents a duplicate.
cases.limitations: Depends on service-side support and workload-specific semantics.

cases.name: tau-bench tool-agent-user evaluation
cases.problem: Measure agents that must interact with users and tools while following domain policy and changing database state.
cases.context: Synthetic retail and airline domains with user simulation, tools and policy constraints.
cases.architecture: Task environment with policy, user simulator, tools and state, evaluated using final database state and response criteria.
cases.approach: Run repeated tasks in a controlled environment and evaluate stateful outcomes.
cases.tradeoffs: Control/reproducibility versus omitted production realities; user simulation may not reflect real interaction.
cases.outcomes: Historical paper results stay in a bounded research sidebar; no score is treated as current model ranking.
cases.lessons: Outcome state and policy must be evaluated, but harness validity constrains the claim.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-09 borrows the idea of policy-plus-state tasks while adding identity, failures, timing and effect ledgers.
cases.limitations: Synthetic benchmark, historical models, domain-specific tasks and assumptions.

cases.name: AgentBench multi-environment evaluation
cases.problem: Compare agent behavior across heterogeneous interactive environments.
cases.context: Eight benchmark environments and historical LLM agents described in the paper.
cases.architecture: Common evaluation framing across multiple environments with environment-specific interactions.
cases.approach: Execute agents in controlled environments and compare task performance.
cases.tradeoffs: Breadth supports contrast, while each environment simplifies production identity, effects and operational constraints.
cases.outcomes: Use only to motivate environment-specific evaluation; do not reproduce stale model rankings as current facts.
cases.lessons: Agent capability is conditional on environment and interface.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-09 satellite portfolio tests whether a method transfers to code, IT access, remedy and research tasks.
cases.limitations: Paper-era results and simplified environments; not production assurance.

cases.name: Anthropic long-running coding-agent harness
cases.problem: Agents working across context windows need to leave usable progress and resume without losing the objective or corrupting the codebase.
cases.architecture: Initializer/progress artifacts, incremental implementation, clean-state checkpoints and verification on each iteration.
cases.approach: Use durable artifacts to make progress inspectable and resumable across agent sessions.
cases.tradeoffs: More structure and verification consume time but reduce opaque restarts and unfinished work.
cases.outcomes: Provider-described experiment; qualitative lessons only unless exact conditions are carried.
cases.lessons: Durable progress artifacts are useful, but external effects still require stronger checkpoint, ownership and reconciliation semantics.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-03/AR-08 use versioned run state and evidence rather than a narrative progress file alone.
cases.limitations: Coding context and local file changes; not a distributed workflow transaction model.

cases.name: MCP elicitation and authorization patterns
cases.problem: A client/server tool ecosystem needs resource-scoped authorization and controlled user interaction without treating sessions or forwarded tokens as identity.
cases.context: MCP 2025-11-25 HTTP authorization and elicitation specifications plus security guidance.
cases.architecture: Protected-resource discovery, OAuth flow, audience-bound tokens, client-mediated elicitation and explicit user response states.
cases.approach: Keep credentials out of form elicitation, bind state to verified users and restrict token audience/scope.
cases.tradeoffs: Interoperability adds discovery and metadata attack surfaces; application approval still needs local meaning.
cases.outcomes: Normative/protocol behavior only; no production outcome claimed.
cases.lessons: Protocol authorization and user interaction are primitives beneath the FieldOps delegation contract.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-05/AR-13 adapter maps protocol identity to local principals and preserves exact synthetic approval semantics.
cases.limitations: Edition-specific; some areas evolve and local effect semantics remain out of scope.

cases.name: A2A task and artifact interoperability
cases.problem: Independent agents need a shared way to discover capabilities and exchange task messages, status and artifacts.
cases.context: A2A v1.0.0 specification and normative protobuf under the Linux Foundation project.
cases.architecture: Agent Cards, Task lifecycle, Messages, Parts, Artifacts, streaming/push and multiple protocol bindings.
cases.approach: Advertise and discover capabilities, exchange versioned task artifacts and track remote task status.
cases.tradeoffs: Common wire semantics improve interoperability but cannot guarantee business-semantic compatibility, trust or local authority.
cases.outcomes: Specification behavior only; no adoption or reliability outcome claimed.
cases.lessons: Keep a local adapter and compatibility tests; do not surrender authority/effect semantics to remote metadata.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-13 simulates a remote inventory specialist whose Agent Card changes; local policy blocks the incompatible capability.
cases.limitations: Main branch can change; publication must pin v1.0.0 tag/commit and verify normative schema.

cases.name: OWASP agentic threat taxonomy and controlled samples
cases.problem: Teams need a shared vocabulary and test prompts for agent-specific threats such as goal hijacking, excessive agency and memory/tool abuse.
cases.context: OWASP GenAI Security Project's 2026 agentic taxonomy and 2025 excessive-agency guidance.
cases.architecture: Risk categories and mitigation guidance used as an input to threat modeling and controlled exercises.
cases.approach: Map relevant categories to local assets, trust boundaries, threat cases and executable controls.
cases.tradeoffs: A common checklist improves coverage prompts but can create false assurance if treated as certification.
cases.lessons: Threat taxonomies generate tests; they do not close residual risk or replace specialist review.
cases.fieldops_use: AR-10 converts applicable categories into deterministic prompt-injection, tenant, scope and approval-bypass fixtures.
cases.limitations: Community guidance, not a standard or complete assurance method.

cases.name: FieldOps Relay synthetic evidence case
cases.problem: Coordinate a fictional equipment service request using synthetic records while preserving approval, effect, recovery and evidence boundaries.
cases.context: Local deterministic sandbox; no network, paid provider, real credential, external system, human contact or equipment control.
cases.architecture: One evolving AR-01 through AR-14 dossier, deterministic model double, narrow local tools, effect ledger, task environment and protocol adapters.
cases.approach: Build and falsify one evidence chain across all 20 chapters, retaining superseded assumptions.
cases.tradeoffs: High reproducibility and safety at the cost of external validity; satellite cases are required for transfer checks.
cases.outcomes: Future executable local test outcomes only. No company, customer, safety or physical-world outcome may be implied.
cases.lessons: The capstone demonstrates methods and evidence structure, not production readiness in a real service domain.
cases.limitations: Fictional, synthetic, low-stakes and deliberately incomplete relative to real scheduling, inventory, labor, safety, legal and operational systems.
